name: Gary Fegel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Gary Fegel ran the aluminum business for Glencore and left the commodities giant in 2013, when he begab building a diversified investment portfolio.
Through his family office GMF Capital, Fegel invests across public and private equity, including companies in media and technology, as well as real estate.
Fegel sold his real estate asset management firm, GMF RE, in 2022.
Fegel's recent deals include the merger of his SPAC with FlyExclusive, a U.S. aviation company, and the purchase of The Motorsport Network, a global media and technology company.
forbes_facts: GMF, the name of Fegel's business, stands for Gary Mischa Fegel.
He and his wife Yael, a lawyer from Britain, have been listed in ARTnet's list of the world's Top 200 collectors.

name: Eric Sprott
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012); Hurun Global (2014-2017); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Eric Sprott is a long time silver and gold bull who has claims to hold 98% of his wealth in the two metals.
The Canadian grew up in Ottawa, the son of a government official who made amateur stock trades in his spare time.
In 1980 Sprott used his savings to buy a seat on the Toronto Stock Exchange and started his own securities firm, Sprott Securities.
He sold his entire interest in Sprott Securities, to the firm's employees in 2001.
Today he manages his family office, holding stakes in 120-plus silver and gold companies.

name: Samuel Barata
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2019-2021); Hurun Global (2020)
forbes_bio: Samuel Barata owns just over half of Drogarias DPSP,  one of Brazil's largest drugstore chains.
The company was formed in the 2011 merger of Drogaria Pacheco, owned by Barata, and Drogaria Sao Paulo, owned the Carvalho family.
The company had 2017 revenues of about $2.4 billion, and has more than 1,000 stores in 10 Brazilian states.
One of Brazil's oldest companies, Drogaria Pacheco was founded in 1892 and acquired by Barata in the 1970s.

name: Julia Oetker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Julia Oetker is an heir to the fortune of the Oetker Group, a now-divided German conglomerate with diverse holdings that included a popular range of food products.
In September of 2024, she gave up her ownership stake in Geschwister Oetker, a German holding company with brands spanning wine and spirits, chemicals and luxury hotels.
Geschwister Oetker was formed in 2021 after the eight Oetker siblings agreed to divide their $8 billion (sales) conglomerate into two separate groups.
The original business, Dr. August Oetker, began in 1891 when her great-grandfather started selling non-perishable baking powder.
Julia's brothers, Alfred and Carl Ferdinand, are co-CEOs and owners of Geschwister Oetker.
forbes_facts: When her father, Rudolf August, passed away in 2007, ownership of Dr. August Oetker was divided between his eight children from three marriages.

name: Marissa Mayer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Google's first female engineer and 20th employee, Marissa Mayer spent 13 years at the tech company, which is the source of much of her fortune.
Mayer took over as CEO of Yahoo in 2012, but was unable to keep web traffic and ad revenues from falling.
Mayer resigned as CEO of Yahoo in 2017, when it sold to Verizon for $4.5 billion, following Yahoo's disclosure of security breaches.
She then cofounded Sunshine, which launched AI apps to automate everyday tasks, in 2018.
Sunshine raised $17 million but is reportedly dissolving and selling its assets to Marissa's third act, AI firm Dazzle.

name: James Truchard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: James Truchard cofounded National Instruments, a supplier of testing and measurement equipment and software for scientists and engineers, in 1976.
A Texas native, he got a PhD in electrical engineering from the University of Texas, Austin in 1974.
He launched National Instruments while working as managing director of the acoustical measurements division at the university's applied research lab.
He retired as chairman in 2019. National Instruments was acquired by manufacturing giant Emerson Electric in 2023.
forbes_facts: A gardening and photography enthusiast, Truchard published "Memories from a Hill Country Garden: Flowers, Stones, and Critters" in 2013.
